A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ε-DPO research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. The retained material can be matched despite additions, reorganization, and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original ε-DPO evaluations on UltraFeedback and Anthropic-HH, including ablations, training analyses, and downstream results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds Qwen2.5 evaluations, wall-time measurements, and an analysis of ε-dependent monotonicity consistency.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(5) and Algorithm 1 retain the same perturbed-policy estimation, instance-level β selection, and batch-mean update. The revised rationale and additional experiments do not change the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback, Anthropic-HH, the same three chatbot benchmarks, and the same six downstream tasks. The added Qwen2.5 experiment changes the model configuration while retaining the task coverage and preference-data construction approach.

E2.justification: The static-β control reporting 75.5% win rate in v2 Table 3 is omitted from the corresponding ablation in v3 Table 5. Original benchmark comparator sets remain; the new Qwen comparison uses the already evaluated SFT, DPO, and SimPO methods.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct using transferred Llama-3 hyperparameters without retuning, a full 3×3 εc/εs grid, wall-time profiling, and a 100-point ε scan at 0.1-epoch checkpoints. Previously reported splits and training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses examine hyperparameter portability, computational overhead, and whether monotonicity decisions remain consistent throughout ε neighborhoods (Figure 5). The split-ε ablation also expands beyond the earlier intersecting sweeps. Existing training-dynamics, KL-frontier, and appendix case analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 4a retains its 95% confidence intervals, and Appendix B retains single-best-model reporting. New Figure 5 extends the existing 95% confidence convention to another analysis; no changed run counts, seeds, statistical tests, or interval-construction procedures are documented.

E6.justification: v3 adds Qwen, timing, ε-consistency, and expanded-grid results. Qwen AlpacaEval LC scores are 42.5% for ε-DPO, 41.6% for DPO, and 32.4% for SimPO. The matched εc=0.02, εs=0.01 ablation changes from 52.4% to 74.2% without explanation. Original benchmark and downstream scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 adds approximate computational-cost reasoning, deriving DPO's 8N FLOPs per token and ε-DPO's relative overhead of approximately 2v/N. Section 3.2 makes the hard-label preference assumption explicit. Proposition 1, its Appendix A proof, and the algorithm's core equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: instance-level adaptive KL control, improved alignment, identification of confusing preference pairs, and efficient KL trade-offs. The new experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an interpretation that SimPO's fixed margin requires adequate retuning when transferring settings, discusses the new approximation-consistency evidence, and acknowledges small nonzero computational overhead. Section 3.2 replaces the numerical-derivative intuition with a hard-label Bradley–Terry rationale; the reference-policy resource limitation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds the Qwen checkpoint source, license, and dataset-construction information. The main text documents hyperparameter transfer and timing measurements. Existing hyperparameter grids, hardware disclosures, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Kaplan et al.'s Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and the Qwen2 technical report. Most other reference changes update existing works to published versions. The related-work organization and central positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 locally rewrites the methodological explanation, organizes experimental subsections by dataset, and updates affiliations, acknowledgements, and publication information. It also inserts a NeurIPS checklist, while retaining the main narrative and Appendix A–D organization.

P2.justification: v3 adds Qwen and timing tables plus Figure 5, and converts the split-ε ablation into a compact matrix. Existing figures and appendix displays are substantially retained, with localized reflow, caption edits, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new transfer experiment, timing measurements, and ε-consistency analysis provide useful support for practical behavior that v2 lacked. These yield a limited net improvement in validation and explanation. The unexplained 52.4% to 74.2% ablation revision and omission of its static control reduce transparency of that comparison and temper the gains.
